title: Possessive adjectives
goal: By the end of this lesson you can say my, your, his, her, our and their in French (mon, ta, ses, notre, leurs…), choose the form by the gender of the thing owned, and talk about your partner and friends the Quebec way: mon chum, ma blonde.

body: Possessive adjectives replace the article (*le, la, les*) and agree with the noun they go with: *mon frère* (my brother), *ma sœur* (my sister), *mes parents* (my parents).
Singular owners have three forms each: masculine, feminine and plural.
Plural owners are simpler: only a singular and a plural form, no gender difference.
*votre / vos* is also the polite 'your' that goes with *vous*: *Votre nom, s'il vous plaît?*
learn.tip: nos‿amis, vos‿enfants, leurs‿enfants: liaison [z] before a vowel.

learn.h: Son or sa? Look at the thing, not the owner
body: This is the big difference from English. *Son / sa* agree with the noun owned, not with the owner. *Sa voiture* can mean his car or her car (voiture is feminine). *Son frère* can mean his brother or her brother.
If the context doesn't make it clear, add *à lui* (his) or *à elle* (hers): *C'est sa voiture à elle.*

body: Before a feminine noun starting with a vowel or silent h, *ma, ta, sa* become *mon, ton, son* to make pronunciation smooth: *mon amie* (my female friend), *ton école*, *son adresse*, *mon histoire*.
Spelling still shows the gender elsewhere: *mon amie est gentille*. To say 'mine', 'yours' with things: *C'est à moi. C'est à toi?*
learn.tip: ma amie ✗ → mon amie ✓ (sounds like mon ami, but written with -e).

body: In Quebec, *mon chum* means 'my boyfriend' (or 'my husband' casually) and *ma blonde* means 'my girlfriend' (or wife), whatever her hair colour! These are the normal everyday words, used by all ages.

*Un chum* can also mean a male friend (*un chum de gars*); a female friend is *une amie* or casually *une chum (de fille)*. For official forms and formal speech: *mon conjoint / ma conjointe* (spouse or common-law partner), *mon copain / ma copine* (boyfriend / girlfriend, more France).

quebec.intro: In Quebec, your boyfriend is mon chum and your girlfriend is ma blonde, regardless of hair colour. Formal forms use conjoint / conjointe.

items.note: informal; context tells boyfriend vs friend
standard in Quebec forms and formal speech

drills.q: 'Paul aime sa mère.' What does 'sa' agree with?
drills.why: Possessives agree with the thing owned.
ma → mon before a feminine vowel; amie keeps its -e.
blonde = girlfriend, whatever her hair colour.

dialogue.fr: C'est ta famille sur la photo?
dialogue.en: Is that your family in the photo?

dialogue.fr: Oui! Là, c'est mes parents, et là, c'est mon frère et sa blonde.
dialogue.en: Yes! There are my parents, and there's my brother and his girlfriend.

dialogue.fr: Et la fille avec les cheveux bruns?
dialogue.en: And the girl with brown hair?

dialogue.fr: C'est ma sœur, Léa. Son chum est à côté.
dialogue.en: That's my sister, Léa. Her boyfriend is next to her.

dialogue.fr: C'est la maison de mes parents, à Sherbrooke.
dialogue.en: It's my parents' house, in Sherbrooke.

dialogue.fr: Ah, c'est le chien de mon frère. Il s'appelle Biscuit!
dialogue.en: Ah, that's my brother's dog. His name is Biscuit!

speak.prompt: Present four people in your life using mon, ma, mes or leur.
speak.model: Mon frère s'appelle Dan. Ma mère habite à Toronto. Mes voisins sont fins. Mon chum travaille à Laval.

speak.prompt: Introduce your partner or a friend the Quebec way.
speak.model: Je te présente ma blonde, Sarah. / Je te présente mon chum, Alex.

speak.prompt: Ask a polite question about someone's name, address and phone number.
speak.model: Quel est votre nom? Quelle est votre adresse? Quel est votre numéro de téléphone?

write.prompt: Write 6 sentences about your family or friends, using at least five different possessive adjectives.
write.model: Mes parents habitent à Toronto. Mon père est professeur et ma mère est infirmière. Ma sœur a deux enfants: leurs noms sont Léo et Emma. Mon amie Sophie habite à Montréal. Son chum est très fin. Notre famille est petite, mais on est proches.
